title: Shannon capacity of \(C_{7}\)
formal: Determine the zero-error Shannon capacity \[\Theta(C_7)=\sup_{t\ge1}\alpha(C_7^{\boxtimes t})^{1/t}\] of the seven-cycle, in distinguishable symbols per channel use, with the graph power defined below.
why: The smallest odd-cycle zero-error capacity left unresolved after Lovasz's pentagon theorem.
status_note: The 31 August 2026 preprint explicitly leaves the exact capacity unresolved. Its reported lower bound and the primary-source upper bound still leave a gap exceeding 0.02, so they do not settle this card’s 0.01 acceptance target. Checked on 13 September 2026; the new construction was not independently verified.

progress.text: Polak and Schrijver give \(\Theta(C_7)\ge367^{1/5}\) and state the Lovász upper bound \(7\cos(\pi/7)/(1+\cos(\pi/7))\).

Tandon’s preprint abstract reports a code in the 500th strong power giving \(\Theta(C_7)\ge3.25883262\ldots\). This is a reported preprint result; the construction and proof were not independently verified.

sentences: The seven-cycle describes which pairs of seven channel symbols can be confused.
Its Shannon capacity is the supremum of independence numbers of strong graph powers raised to the reciprocal power.
The card asks for this real number in distinguishable symbols per use, rather than bits per use.
No finite graph power is assumed to attain the supremum.
The Lean benchmark accepts an explicit value with certified absolute error at most 0.01.

definitions: \(C_{7}\) has vertex set \(\{0,\ldots ,6\}\), with distinct vertices adjacent when their difference modulo 7 is 1 or 6. For an integer \(t\ge 1\), the strong power has vertex set \(\{0,\ldots ,6\}^{t}\). Two distinct tuples are adjacent when, in every coordinate, their entries are equal or adjacent in \(C_{7}\). An independent set contains no adjacent distinct pair, and \(\alpha\) is its maximum cardinality. The capacity is measured in distinguishable symbols per channel use, rather than its logarithm in bits. It lies between 3 and 7; the supremum need not occur at a finite power. There is no computational restriction on independent sets or their construction.
answer_criterion: Supply a specified real number \(a\) and a Lean proof that \(|a-\Theta(C_7)|\le1/100\). Certified lower and upper bounds \(\ell\le\Theta(C_7)\le u\) with \(u-\ell\le1/50\) qualify by taking \(a=(\ell+u)/2\). An exact value with proof also qualifies. A restatement of the defining supremum, a one-sided bound or an estimate without certified error does not suffice. This tolerance concerns the benchmark value, not an exact-capacity conjecture.

context_blocks.text: The seven-cycle is the first odd cycle after the pentagon whose exact zero-error capacity remains unresolved in the cited literature. Independent sets in its strong powers represent collections of mutually distinguishable codewords.

The August 2026 preprint reports a lower bound of \(3.25883262\ldots\), while the Lovász upper bound is \(7\cos(\pi/7)/(1+\cos(\pi/7))\approx3.31766720\). Their gap is still larger than \(1/50\), so these bounds do not yet meet this card’s acceptance tolerance.
